title: Hammamet’s Dar Sebastian: guides say Rommel stayed there; the record is thinner
body: **Dar Sebastian** in Hammamet is the villa that George Sebastian, born in Romania, had built around 1930 (sources give 1927 to 1934), in a garden of about ten hectares by the sea. He sold it to the Tunisian state in the 1960s; it is now the International Cultural Centre of Hammamet, whose open-air theatre President Habib Bourguiba opened in 1964 and which hosts the Hammamet festival each summer. Guides often say Rommel used it as his headquarters. The Tunisian writer Hatem Bourial, who has written its history, says Sebastian left in 1939 and that the German army requisitioned the house; of Rommel he writes only that he “may even have spent a few nights” there. The dates are tight: Rommel took command of Army Group Africa in Tunisia on 23 February 1943 and left Africa on 9 March. None of these sources cites a wartime document. The same goes for the story, repeated by Tunisia’s news agency without a date, that Winston Churchill wrote part of his memoirs here. Enjoy the house and garden, and weigh the war stories source by source. Check opening times locally.

slides.alt: Animation: a white villa with arcades and a small dome in a green garden by the sea at Hammamet, an open-air theatre beside it. Paper cards stamped DOCUMENTED, REPORTED or TOLD appear one by one; a date bar from November 1942 to May 1943 marks 23 February to 9 March 1943.

slides.prompt: Slide through 1942–43. Find the last day on which Rommel could have slept at Dar Sebastian.
slides.takeaway: 9 March 1943: he left Africa that day for good. The story can fit only a few weeks of early 1943, and no wartime document in the sources shows it. Dates can rule a story out.
